# Clamping Device for a Light Guide

## Overview

A clamping device for securing a light guide is provided, comprising a carrier structure equipped with two securing elements. These securing elements are configured to hold the light guide firmly in place at two distinct positions, ensuring stable and reliable fixation of the light guide within the device.

## Configuration of the Securing Elements

The clamping device includes a first securing element and a second securing element, which are arranged in a spaced-apart relationship relative to one another. This deliberate spacing establishes two separate securing positions along the light guide. As a result, the two securing positions are separated by a first distance measured along the longitudinal extension of the light guide. This arrangement allows the light guide to be held at two defined points, distributing the clamping forces and maintaining the intended orientation of the light guide.

## The Intermediate Carrier

To facilitate mounting and application, the device further incorporates an intermediate carrier. This intermediate carrier features a first surface and an opposing second surface. The securing elements are attached to the first surface, thereby anchoring the light guide to the carrier structure. The second surface, situated opposite the first, is specifically designed to be applied to a measurement object, enabling the device to be positioned precisely against the surface or component to be measured.

## Geometric Relationship of the Securing Positions

A notable characteristic of this configuration concerns the spacing of the securing positions as defined on the intermediate carrier. Specifically, the distance between the securing positions on the intermediate carrier is greater than the first distance measured along the longitudinal direction of the light guide. This intentional difference in spacing accommodates the geometry of the light guide and the measurement object, allowing the light guide to be routed and secured in a manner that optimizes both mechanical stability and measurement performance.

## Summary

In summary, the described clamping device combines a carrier structure, two spaced-apart securing elements, and an intermediate carrier with dual surfaces to provide a robust and precise means of fixing a light guide relative to a measurement object. The particular relationship between the securing distances further enhances the adaptability and functional reliability of the device.

# Clamping Device for a Light Guide

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a clamping device for securing a light guide, and more particularly to a device that enables precise and controlled positioning of a light guide relative to a measurement object. Such devices find application in optical measurement systems where the accurate placement of light-conducting elements is essential for reliable data acquisition.

## Background and Purpose

In many optical measurement applications, a light guide must be brought into a defined spatial relationship with a surface or object to be examined. The quality of the measurement often depends critically on the geometry of this arrangement, including the spacing and orientation of the light guide with respect to the measurement surface. Conventional mounting arrangements frequently lack the ability to control this positioning in a repeatable and mechanically robust manner, which can lead to measurement inaccuracies or inconsistent results.

## Description of the Device

The clamping device according to the present description addresses these challenges through the use of a dedicated carrier structure. This carrier structure incorporates two securing elements that are arranged in a spaced-apart relationship to one another. These securing elements are responsible for holding the light guide firmly in place at two distinct locations along its length.

The securing elements are mounted on an intermediate carrier, which serves as the central structural component of the device. The intermediate carrier is provided with two functional surfaces. The first surface is configured to receive and hold the light guide, thereby establishing the interface between the carrier and the optical element. The second surface, which lies opposite the first, is intended for application against the measurement object. In this way, the intermediate carrier acts as a bridge between the light guide on one side and the object under investigation on the other.

## Key Feature and Advantages

The distinguishing feature of this clamping device lies in the geometric relationship between the securing positions. Specifically, the distance between the securing positions on the intermediate carrier—that is, the locations at which the securing elements are attached to the carrier—is deliberately made greater than the distance between the positions at which the light guide itself is secured.

This dimensional relationship produces a defined mechanical effect on the light guide. Because the mounting points on the carrier are spaced farther apart than the corresponding points at which the light guide is held, the light guide is subjected to a controlled geometric constraint. This arrangement allows the position and orientation of the light guide to be established in a precise and predictable manner relative to the measurement object.

As a result, the device enables controlled positioning of the light guide, ensuring that it is consistently brought into the desired relationship with the surface or object being measured. This controlled positioning enhances the reliability and repeatability of the optical measurements, while the two-point securing arrangement provides a stable and robust mechanical mounting for the light guide.

# Patent Claim

**1.** A clamping device for securing a light guide, comprising:

a first securing element arranged at a first position and configured to engage the light guide;

a second securing element arranged at a second position spaced apart from the first position along a longitudinal extent of the light guide, the second securing element being configured to engage the light guide; and

an intermediate carrier disposed between the first securing element and the second securing element, the intermediate carrier supporting the light guide along a portion thereof extending between the first position and the second position,

wherein the intermediate carrier is configured to be attached to a measurement object such that the light guide is held in a predetermined position relative to the measurement object by the first securing element, the second securing element, and the intermediate carrier.

---

### Suggested Dependent Claims

**2.** The clamping device according to claim 1, wherein the first securing element and the second securing element each comprise a clamping jaw configured to exert a retaining force on the light guide.

**3.** The clamping device according to claim 1, wherein the intermediate carrier comprises a mounting surface configured to be affixed to a surface of the measurement object.

**4.** The clamping device according to claim 1, wherein the intermediate carrier defines a guide channel receiving the portion of the light guide extending between the first position and the second position.

**5.** The clamping device according to claim 1, wherein at least one of the first securing element and the second securing element is adjustable relative to the intermediate carrier to vary a tension applied to the light guide.

---

# SUMMARY

The present invention provides an optical fiber clamping apparatus that addresses the aforementioned deficiencies in the prior art by providing a reliable, low-stress mechanism for securing an optical fiber (10) during splicing, inspection, or termination operations.

In accordance with one aspect of the present invention, an optical fiber clamping apparatus (100) is provided, comprising a base member (12) having a longitudinally extending V-groove (14) configured to receive and align the optical fiber (10). A clamping arm (16) is pivotally coupled to the base member (12) by a hinge (18), the clamping arm (16) being movable between an open position, in which the optical fiber (10) may be inserted into the V-groove (14), and a closed position, in which the optical fiber (10) is retained within the V-groove (14).

In accordance with another aspect of the present invention, the clamping arm (16) carries a resilient clamping pad (20) that engages the optical fiber (10) when the clamping arm (16) is in the closed position. The resilient clamping pad (20) distributes clamping force along the optical fiber (10), thereby reducing localized stress concentrations and minimizing the risk of microbending losses or fiber breakage.

In accordance with a further aspect of the present invention, a biasing member (22), such as a spring, urges the clamping arm (16) toward the closed position, thereby maintaining a substantially constant clamping force on the optical fiber (10). In certain embodiments, an actuator (24) is operatively coupled to the clamping arm (16) to selectively move the clamping arm (16) against the bias of the biasing member (22) to the open position.

In accordance with yet another aspect of the present invention, the base member (12) includes a latching mechanism (26) that releasably secures the clamping arm (16) in the closed position, thereby ensuring that the optical fiber (10) remains reliably retained during handling and processing.

Additionally, the base member (12) may be formed from a thermally stable material to maintain alignment accuracy across a range of operating temperatures.

It is an object of the present invention to provide an optical fiber clamping apparatus (100) that securely retains an optical fiber (10) while minimizing mechanical stress imparted thereto.

It is a further object of the present invention to provide an optical fiber clamping apparatus (100) that is simple to operate, permitting rapid insertion and removal of the optical fiber (10).
